description: Use your Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription in VS Code: chat models, an @m365 chat participant, editor and Source Control actions, agent tools and inline completions. Available in English and Spanish.
tool.m365ListFiles.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot list workspace files.
tool.m365SearchText.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot search text in the workspace.
tool.m365ReadFile.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot read workspace files.
tool.m365ApplyEdits.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot propose changes in the workspace (with review and diff).
tool.m365GetDiagnostics.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot read the errors/warnings VS Code already shows.
tool.m365GitInfo.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot query git (status/diff/log) without changing anything.
tool.m365GenerateCommitMessage.userDescr: Lets M365 Copilot trigger VS Code’s native commit message generation.
tool.m365GitCommit.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot create a commit (after you confirm the exact message).
tool.m365RunCommand.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot run a terminal command (after you confirm it).
tool.m365SpawnAgents.userDescription: Lets M365 Copilot delegate tasks to sub-agents (in parallel) to explore or modify the workspace.
config.language.auto: Follow VS Code’s display language (Spanish for any Spanish locale, English otherwise).
config.language: Language of M365 Copilot’s messages, status bar, tool results — and of the instructions sent to the model, which is what makes it answer in that language. Applies immediately. Command titles and these setting descriptions always follow VS Code’s own display language.
config.notifications.tokenExpiry: Warn when the token is about to expire without having been renewed, and when it expires during the session, with buttons to paste a new one or open M365 Copilot. The status bar always shows the token state.
config.editor.codeActions: Offer M365 Copilot actions in the lightbulb: **Fix** on errors and warnings (edited in place, with Keep/Undo), and **Edit…**, **Explain** and **Document** on a selection.
config.tools.includeEditorTools: Also describe VS Code’s own tools (agent mode, MCP and other extensions) to the model, not only this extension’s. That is what lets the agent read, edit or run things with the editor’s native tools. Turn it off to go back to the previous behaviour (only `m365_*` tools).
config.tools.duplicates.preferEditor: When a native tool does the same as one of ours, the model is told to use the native one.
config.tools.duplicates.preferM365: The other way round: this extension’s tools are preferred (workspace-relative paths and its own Keep/Undo review).
config.tools.duplicates.both: No preference is stated; the model chooses.
config.tools.duplicates: Which tool to prefer when one of ours and a native VS Code one do the same thing (read, search, edit, terminal…). Neither is hidden: the other stays available as a fallback if the preferred one fails.
config.tools.maxAdvertised: Maximum number of tools described in the prompt. BizChat has no native function calling: the catalog travels as text, so with many active tools (MCP included) it is worth capping. Tools that are not described can still be run if the model names them.
config.subagents.enabled: Let the model delegate tasks to sub-agents (`m365_spawn_agents`): each one runs its own tool loop — including edits and commands, with the usual Keep/Undo review and confirmation — and only returns a summary. Turn it off and the tool does nothing (it explains why instead of running).
config.subagents.maxConcurrent: How many sub-agents can run at the same time when several tasks are delegated. The rest wait their turn; calls that edit files or run commands are always serialised among themselves (max. 1 at a time) so they do not step on each other.
config.subagents.maxSteps: Maximum number of tool calls a sub-agent can make before returning a partial summary with a limit-reached warning.
config.subagents.model: Model (tone) used by sub-agents, independent of the one selected in the main chat.
config.inlineCompletions.enabled: Inline code suggestions (ghost text) with M365 Copilot. **Note:** every suggestion is a request against your M365 plan, and latency is ~1-3 s (BizChat opens a new WebSocket per request and is not a completion model). If it feels slow or costly, use `triggerMode: manual`.
config.inlineCompletions.triggerMode.aut: Suggest only after you stop typing (with the debounceMs delay).
config.inlineCompletions.triggerMode.man: Suggest only when you ask for it (Alt+\ by default in VS Code).
config.inlineCompletions.triggerMode: When to request suggestions. “manual” greatly reduces quota usage.
config.inlineCompletions.debounceMs: Milliseconds without typing before requesting a suggestion. Higher uses less quota; lower answers sooner but fires more requests.
config.inlineCompletions.maxLines: Maximum lines per suggestion. Fewer lines = less latency.
config.inlineCompletions.timeoutMs: Maximum wait per suggestion. Past that point it is discarded: a late suggestion gets in the way more than it helps.
config.inlineCompletions.model: Model used for inline completions. “reasoning” is noticeably slower; not recommended here.
config.inlineCompletions.disabledLanguag: Language ids where ghost text is never requested automatically (an explicit `Alt+\` still works). `scminput` is the Source Control commit box. Every suggestion costs a request, so leave out languages where it does not help.

walkthrough.title: Get started with M365 Copilot
walkthrough.description: Connect your Microsoft 365 Copilot account and use it from the chat, the editor and Source Control.
walkthrough.capture.title: Capture your token in the browser
walkthrough.capture.description:
Install the M365 Copilot browser extension (Chrome, Edge or Firefox) and open Microsoft 365 Copilot once. It captures your session token and keeps it in sync with VS Code automatically.
[Download the browser extension](https://github.com/cristiancastineiras/M365CopilotVSCode/releases)
No browser extension? The Tampermonkey userscript in the repository copies the token for you.
walkthrough.capture.alt: The browser extension popup, showing the token and VS Code connection status.
walkthrough.paste.title: Paste the token (only without the browser extension)
walkthrough.paste.description:
With the browser extension the token arrives by itself. Otherwise, copy it and paste it here — it is stored encrypted in VS Code’s SecretStorage. The **Accounts** menu (bottom of the activity bar) shows who is signed in, signs you in when there is no token and signs you out.
[Paste profile or token](command:m365copilot.pasteProfile)
walkthrough.paste.alt: The input box where the token is pasted.
walkthrough.chat.title: Chat with M365 Copilot
walkthrough.chat.description:
Type **@m365** in the chat, or pick an **M365 Copilot** model in the model picker (Auto, GPT, Claude Sonnet, Reasoning…). In agent mode it can read, edit and run things in your workspace, always with your review.
[Open chat with @m365](command:m365copilot.openChat)
walkthrough.chat.alt: The M365 Copilot models in the chat model picker.
walkthrough.editor.title: Use it from the editor
walkthrough.editor.description:
Select code and press **Ctrl+Shift+Alt+I** (or right-click → **M365 Copilot → Edit code…**) to change it with an instruction, right there. The lightbulb offers **Fix with M365 Copilot** on errors, and the same menu explains, documents or tests code. Every change is highlighted block by block with **Keep / Undo**. In Source Control, ✨ writes the commit message; in the terminal, right-click → **Explain last terminal command**.
[Edit the code at the cursor](command:m365copilot.editCode)
walkthrough.editor.alt: An agent edit highlighted in the editor with Keep and Undo.
walkthrough.language.title: English or Spanish
walkthrough.language.description:
M365 Copilot follows VS Code’s display language by default. Change it at any time — it also changes the language of the instructions sent to the model.
[Change language](command:m365copilot.selectLanguage)
participant.command.terminal: Explain the last terminal command (its output and exit code) and how to fix it
config.editor.model: Model (tone) for the answers written straight into the editor: **Edit code…**, the lightbulb’s **Fix with M365 Copilot** and the Source Control commit message.
config.terminal.captureOutput: Keep, in memory, the output and exit code of the last commands of each terminal (requires VS Code’s shell integration), so `@m365 /terminal` and **Explain last terminal command** can explain them. Nothing is sent anywhere until you ask.
config.models.updateFromCatalog: Download the list of M365 Copilot models from the project’s online catalog (`models.json` on GitHub) on start and every 12 hours, so new models appear — and retired ones disappear — without updating the extension. Only that file is downloaded; nothing is sent.
config.models.detectFromBrowser: Add the models the M365 Copilot web app itself uses: the browser extension and the userscript see which model (`tone`) each chat uses and send it along with the token. Proof that the model exists for your account.
config.models.custom: Extra models by their BizChat `tone`, e.g. `["Gpt_5_7_Chat", { "tone": "Claude_Opus", "name": "Claude Opus" }]`. Use it to try a model before it reaches the catalog.
command.fixAllProblems: Fix all problems in this file
walkthrough.review.title: Code review as comments
walkthrough.review.description:
Right-click → **M365 Copilot → Review code** reviews the selection or the file, and the ☑ button in Source Control reviews your uncommitted changes. Findings appear as comments on the lines (and in the **Comments** panel), each with **Apply fix** and **Dismiss**. With several errors in a file, the lightbulb also offers **Fix all problems in this file**.
[Review the current file](command:m365copilot.reviewCode)
tool.m365SearchProject.userDescription: Finds the most relevant code of the workspace in the local project index (RAG).
tool.m365ProjectMap.userDescription: The project structure, or a file’s outline, imports and importers, from the local project index.
tool.m365WebSearch.userDescription: Searches the internet through Microsoft 365 Copilot and returns the answer with its sources.
config.index.enabled: Keep a local index of the workspace (files, symbols, imports, code chunks) so M365 Copilot understands the project: it adds the relevant code to each request and gives the agent `m365_search_project` and `m365_project_map`. Nothing leaves the machine except the code included in a request.
config.index.maxFiles: Maximum number of files in the project index (source code first).
config.index.maxFileKB: Files larger than this (in KB) are not indexed.
config.index.exclude: Extra glob patterns left out of the project index (in addition to `.gitignore`, `files.exclude` and `search.exclude`), e.g. `**/fixtures/**`.
config.context.autoRetrieve: Add the most relevant project code (from the project index) and a short project map to every chat request.
config.context.maxChars: Maximum size, in characters, of the project context added to a request.
config.web.enabled: Let M365 Copilot search the internet: through the `m365_web_search` tool (agent and `@m365`), and directly in chat requests that use no tools. Needs the session captured by the browser extension or the userscript.
